summary: Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1965–1969, doctorate 1998). He served at Komazawa University from 1984 as lecturer, associate professor, professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019), and worked at Soto Zen Research Center.

Masataka Suzuki specializes in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Keio University (~1968–1978) and held a post there (~1982–2015). In 2026, he was attested as a lecturer at ICPBS and IIBS.

Masato Kobayashi is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Kyoto University (~1989–1995) and under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania (~1995–2000, PhD). He served as a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2003).

Masatoshi Konishi (1938–2020) was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He studied at ICU, University of Calcutta, University of Tokyo, and Rikkyo University (doctorate 2009). He taught at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003, professor emeritus).

Masatoshi Nagatomi (1926–2000) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku, Kyoto (BA ~1947–1950), and Harvard (PhD ~1951–1957). He served at Harvard University as instructor (1958) and professor (1969), and at Harvard Divinity School (~1969–1996).

Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history who studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1980). He held academic posts at Kansai University (~1985–1995), Osaka University (~1995–2017), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2017).

Masayuki Tsukimoto specializes in Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. In 2026, he was attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Massimo Pallottino (1909–1995) was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1927–1931) and later held academic positions at the University of Cagliari (~1940–1945) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1947–1980).

Masumi Mochizuki is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He has held appointments at Minobusan University, attested as a lecturer in 2001, professor in 2015, and special appointment professor in 2026.

Mathieu Boisvert works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied under A. K. Warder and Ravindra Panth. He founded and, in 1992, became a professor at the Université du Québec à Montréal.
Matteo Bartoli (1873–1946) was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1894–1898) and under Heinrich Hübschmann. He held a post at the University of Turin from ~1908 to 1946.

Matthew Orsborn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2012) under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. In 2026, he held a post at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Matthew R. Sayers specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Brereton and Patrick Olivelle (attested 2008), and held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, IUC, Osaka City University, and Duke University (PhD attested 2015) under Richard M. Jaffe, Helen J. Baroni, Michel Mohr, and Amy Allocco.

Matthew T. Kapstein is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD at Brown University (1980–1987). His posts include the University of Chicago, Columbia University (~1989–1996), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2002).

Matthew W. King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Toronto by 2014 under Frances Garrett, having also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thupten Champa.

Matthias Alexander Castrén (1813–1852) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki / Imperial Alexander University (~1830–1836) and held a post there from ~1851 to 1852.
Matthias de Vries (1820–1892) was a scholar in linguistics. He studied at Leiden University (~1838–1843) and held posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891).

Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) was a linguist and Indologist. Educated at Graz and Erlangen-Nuremberg, he held posts at St. Anne's Gymnasium (1855–1857), University of Freiburg (~1868–1870), University of Würzburg (1868), and University of Munich (1890).

Matthieu Ricard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a doctorate at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob (~1967–1972), studied under Kangyour and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoches, founded Karuna-Shechen, and is a Mind and Life board member.
